projects.name: Self-hosted HA Kubernetes Platform
projects.description: A proof of concept: three desktop PCs running a highly available k3s cluster (embedded etcd, so it keeps working if one node goes down), set up with Ansible. CI builds the image and updates the tag in a Helm config repo, then Argo CD syncs the change to the cluster. Secrets live in a self-hosted Infisical and reach pods through its Kubernetes operator. Traefik handles ingress and TLS, and Argo CD and Infisical are only reachable from the LAN. I kept a log of the 28 problems I hit and how I fixed each one.

nodes.label: Users
nodes.note: Only ports 80 and 443 are open. The Kubernetes API isn't exposed; I use a VPN for remote admin.

nodes.label: Traefik
nodes.note: Runs as a DaemonSet with externalTrafficPolicy: Local so it sees real client IPs. An IP allowlist keeps Argo CD and Infisical LAN-only. TLS certs come from a local mkcert CA.

nodes.label: Git repo
nodes.note: Private repo with the Helm chart and values. Argo CD reads it with a read-only deploy key.

nodes.label: Argo CD
nodes.note: Renders the Helm chart and syncs automatically with prune and self-heal, so manual changes in the cluster get reverted.

nodes.label: App pods
nodes.note: A Spring Boot service from a private registry. It gets its config as env vars from a Kubernetes Secret and restarts automatically when a secret changes.

nodes.label: Infisical
nodes.note: Self-hosted secrets manager with PostgreSQL and Redis, installed with Helm. No secret values in Git.

nodes.label: Operator
nodes.note: Logs in to Infisical with a machine identity and copies a secrets folder into a Kubernetes Secret, using the in-cluster service address.

nodes.label: Source repo
nodes.note: App code, in a separate repo from the Helm config.

nodes.label: git push main
nodes.note: Pushing to the target branch starts the pipeline.

nodes.label: Build/test/push
nodes.note: Runs tests, builds the Docker image and pushes it to the private registry, tagged with the commit SHA.

nodes.label: Clone config
nodes.note: Checks out the config repo with a token that can only push to that repo. CI has no access to the cluster.

nodes.label: Bump Helm tag
nodes.note: Updates image.tag in the service's values.yaml, then commits and pushes. If another build pushed first, it rebases and retries.

nodes.label: Argo CD
nodes.note: Picks up the new commit in the config repo and renders the chart again. CI never talks to the Kubernetes API.

nodes.label: Cluster sync
nodes.note: Applies the change with prune and self-heal. To roll back, revert the tag commit.

nodes.label: Rolling update
nodes.note: New pods replace the old ones one at a time. Secrets still come from the Infisical Operator.

projects.name: DevOps Pipeline & Kubernetes Research
projects.description: Compared kubeadm, kind, minikube and k3s on RAM and CPU use, and picked k3s for low-resource servers. Then built a build, test and deploy pipeline for Java and React apps on a self-hosted k3s cluster, with Grafana, VictoriaMetrics and Loki for metrics and logs.

nodes.label: git push
nodes.note: Java and React apps. Every push to main starts the pipeline.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions
nodes.note: Build, test and deploy jobs. Docker images are built in CI.

nodes.label: k3s cluster
nodes.note: Self-hosted k3s, picked after comparing kubeadm, kind, minikube and k3s on RAM and CPU use.

nodes.label: VictoriaMetrics
nodes.note: Uses less memory than Prometheus on small servers and still accepts Prometheus queries.

nodes.label: Loki
nodes.note: Collects logs from every app on the cluster.

nodes.label: Grafana
nodes.note: Dashboards for deployments and logs.

projects.name: Automated Receipt Processing
projects.description: A serverless expense tracker on AWS. Uploading a receipt image to S3 triggers a Lambda function. Textract reads the fields and line items (over 95% accuracy), the results go into DynamoDB, and SES emails the user a summary.

nodes.label: S3 upload
nodes.note: Uploading a receipt image here triggers the Lambda function.

nodes.label: Lambda
nodes.note: Python function that calls Textract, saves the results and sends the email.

nodes.label: Textract
nodes.note: Reads key-value pairs and line items from receipt images, with over 95% accuracy.

nodes.label: DynamoDB
nodes.note: Stores the parsed receipt data.

nodes.label: SES
nodes.note: Emails the user what was read from the receipt.
